possibilities for them? Please chart out the sequence of events timeline between the manifestations of each of these problems and current outcomes.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E1. Pain in the epigastric region\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EIt may be due to -\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EA. Myocardial Infarction\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EB. Acute Pancreatitis\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EC. Cholecystitis\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003ED. Peptic Ulcer\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EE. Acid Reflux Disease\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EF. Gastritis\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E2. Shortness of Breath\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EIt may be due to -\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EA. Acidosis due to renal failure\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EB. Pleural Effusion\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E3. Decreased Urine output\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EA. It may be due to renal failure\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EB. Secondary to acute pancreatitis\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003ERelease of pancreatic amylase from the injured pancreas with resulting impairment of renal microcirculation, decrease in renal perfusion pressure due to abdominal compartment syndrome, intra-abdominal hypertension and hypovolemia.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC6041506\/\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E4. Abdominal distention with constipation and nausea\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EThis may be due to -\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EBowel complications of acute pancreatitis such as paralytic ileus, ischemic necrosis, perforation and mechanical obstruction\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EThis is believed to stem from either:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E1) severe inflammation of the body and tail of the pancreas causing extrinsic compression;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E2) retroperitoneal extravasation of pancreatic enzymes causing pericolitis and\/or pericolic fibrosis;\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E3) thrombosis of mesenteric arteries (often associated with hypercoagulability during severe inflammatory states); or\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E4) infarction\/ischemic necrosis of watershed areas secondary to systemic hypotension. Retroperitoneal inflammation may also lead to the involvement of other segments of bowel including the small intestine\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC5330692\/\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"\u0026quot;.SFUI-Regular\u0026quot;\"\u003EDuring the first 1-2 wk, a pro-inflammatory response occurs, which results in systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS), a sterile response in which sepsis or infection rarely occurs. If the SIRS is severe, then proinflammatory mediators can cause early multiple (respiratory, cardiovascular, renal, and hepatic) organ failure\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"\u0026quot;.SFUI-Regular\u0026quot;\"\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"\u0026quot;.SFUI-Regular\u0026quot;\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC4194569\/\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"\u0026quot;.SFUI-Regular\u0026quot;\"\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"\u0026quot;.SFUI-Regular\u0026quot;\"\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"\u0026quot;.SFUI-Regular\u0026quot;\"\u003ESequence of events\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"\u0026quot;.SFUI-Regular\u0026quot;\"\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"\u0026quot;.SFUI-Regular\u0026quot;\"\u003E1.Diaphyseal dysplasia of both tibia\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"\u0026quot;.SFUI-Regular\u0026quot;\"\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"\u0026quot;.SFUI-Regular\u0026quot;\"\u003E2. Patient is a alcoholic and smoker since 30years\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"\u0026quot;.SFUI-Regular\u0026quot;\"\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"\u0026quot;.SFUI-Regular\u0026quot;\"\u003E3. Patient has an atherosclerotic vascular disease of right upper limb\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"\u0026quot;.SFUI-Regular\u0026quot;\"\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"\u0026quot;.SFUI-Regular\u0026quot;\"\u003E4. Patient presented with chest pain,sob, decreased urine output(due to AKI secondary to sepsis),constipation(due to paralytic ileus),abdominal distension\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"\u0026quot;.SFUI-Regular\u0026quot;\"\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"\u0026quot;.SFUI-Regular\u0026quot;\"\u003EHe was diagnosed with acute severe pancreatitis\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"\u0026quot;.SFUI-Regular\u0026quot;\"\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"\u0026quot;.SFUI-Regular\u0026quot;\"\u003E5. Patient was started on inj.lasix and iv antibiotics and after 1 day pedal edema and sob decreased, the next day, patient was\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"\u0026quot;.SFUI-Regular\u0026quot;\"\u003Ein altered sensorium and was taken for hemodialysis and serum creatinine decreased\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"\u0026quot;.SFUI-Regular\u0026quot;\"\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"\u0026quot;.SFUI-Regular\u0026quot;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;6. After 2days patient was taken for next session of dialysis\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"\u0026quot;.SFUI-Regular\u0026quot;\"\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"\u0026quot;.SFUI-Regular\u0026quot;\"\u003E7. Within 24hrs of 2nd session of dialysis his creat increased again to 5.4 and patient had 8episodes of vomitings and was intolerant to oral feeds.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EB)\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1)Fluid replacement\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIncreased vascular permeability in acute pancreatitis causes the loss of intravenous fluid and reduces plasma volume. Patients should be monitered closely for early detection of respiratory failure\u003C\/p\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv data-maxwidth=\"\" data-minwidth=\"\" data-width=\"340px\" dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"roboto, sans-serif\"\u003E2) A 55 year old male, shepherd by occupation, presented to the OPD with the chief complaints of fever (on and off), loss of appetite, headache, body pains, generalized weakness since 2 months, cough since 2 weeks and vomitings and pain abdomen since 2 days.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"roboto, sans-serif\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"roboto, sans-serif\"\u003E\u003Ca data-saferedirecturl=\"https:\/\/www.google.com\/url?hl=en\u0026amp;q=https:\/\/aakansharaj.blogspot.com\/2020\/11\/55-year-old-male-with-anemia.html?m%3D1\u0026amp;source=gmail\u0026amp;ust=1604938292505000\u0026amp;usg=AFQjCNF9l6YhnWa2dLomcXINpecbtlHsgg\" href=\"https:\/\/aakansharaj.blogspot.com\/2020\/11\/55-year-old-male-with-anemia.html?m=1\" target=\"_blank\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/aakansharaj.blogspot.\u003Cwbr\u003Ecom\/2020\/11\/55-year-old-male-\u003Cwbr\u003Ewith-anemia.html?m=1\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"roboto, sans-serif\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003Ea) Where are the different anatomical locations of the patient's problems and what are the different etiologic possibilities for them? welcome.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHere's a case that I have seen -\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EA 55 year old male, shepherd by occupation, presented to the days.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe patient was apparently assymptommatic 2 months back\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThen he developed fever which was insidious in onset, low grade fever, intermittent type.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EIt is associated with chills and rigors\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThere are no aggravating factors and the fever was relieved on taking medication\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E(For which he visited the RMP)\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EIt is associated with generalized weakness, headache (diffuse), neck pain, loss of appetite and weight loss.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EIt is associated with cough since 2 weeks\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EIt is productive in nature. The sputum is mild in quantity, white in colour, non-purulent, non-blood stained, non-foul smelling.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EH\/O shortness of breath on exertion\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EH\/O vomitings since 2 days\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E1 episode\/day containing ingested food particles.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENon-bilious, non-blood stained, non-projectile\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EH\/O pain abdomen since 2 days in the right hypochondrium, non- radiating\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENo H\/O loose stools\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENo H\/O chest pain, palpitations, orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal appetite\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAdequate sleep\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ERegular bowel and bladder movements\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ERegular intake of alcohol and beedi Features of pleural fluid cytology suggestive of Acute Inflammation.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EBone Marrow Biopsy-\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESite - Sternum\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EParticles - Aspirated 2 ml of blood mixed marrow\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ECellularity - Hypercellular M : E ratio = 2:1\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EErythropoiesis - Erythropoiesis suppressed with Normoblastic proliferation. Few megaloblasts are seen.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EMyelopoiesis - Mild myelosuppression seen with orderly maturation\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EMegakaryopoiesis - Normal with few hypolobated forms seen\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ELymphocytes and Plasma cells -\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ELymphocytes - Normal to increased in number\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPlasma cells - Plasmacytosis with approximately 30% mature plasma cells seen showing abundant basophilic cytoplasm, eccentric nucleus with characteristic cart wheel chromatin perinuclear hoff binucleate forms, mott cells with russell bodies and occassional plasmablasts seen.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EIron stain - Grade 2 (Normal iron stores)\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EImpression - Mild suppression of myeloid and erythroid series. Megakaryopoiesis within normal limits. Plasmacytosis seen (30%) showing mature plasma cells. Indicative of most probably plasma cells dyscrasias.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\n \u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEgh906g7pPuqBvELTlL_0tav5gb2bYGn_2UdvLXGOKoU22qrFgxeDCPvzwLMI-q2iXs3_fZCwaN44AmyuZH84HRBc9MZn9iNl_-RryzdGBLC-QeozqHZJJTaDQrbng4TggIinuj7wEY9aI\/s1600\/1605594222046460-0.png\" imageanchor=\"1\" style=\"margin-left: 1em; Year Old Male with Pedal Oedema and Shortness of Breath"},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThis is an online E log book to discuss our patient's de-identified health data shared after taking his\/her\/guardian's signed informed consent.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHere we discuss our individual patient's problems through series of inputs from available global online community of experts with an aim to solve those patient's clinical problems with collective current best evidence based inputs.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThis E log book also reflects my patient-centered online learning portfolio and your valuable inputs on the comment box is welcome.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHere's a case that I have seen -\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EA 35 year old labourer, a father of two, presented to the OPD with the complaints of pedal oedema (upto the ankle) facial puffiness and abdominal discomfort since 3 days.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHe was apparently assymptomatic 3 months back. Then he developed pedal oedema for the first time for which he visited the RMP who prescribed Torsemide. The oedema subsided after taking the medication. The patient got the confidence that it will decrease everytime after taking the medication so he continued consuming alcohol and taking that medicine everytime he got developed oedema (3-4 times according to the patient and more than that according to the attender)\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe pedal oedema was bilateral, gradual in onset, non-progressive, pitting type, non-tender.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe pedal oedema was followed by facial puffiness.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHe has H\/O chest trauma on the right side of the chest 1 month back (He fell from the bike after consuming alcohol) after which he developed chest pain on the right side of the chest and palpitations on and off.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHe last consumed alcohol 5 days ago after which he developed pedal oedema and facial puffiness again. He even developed abdominal discomfort and shortness of breath at rest. He visited the RMP again who advised him to go to Kamineni, Narketpally.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPast History -\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPatient had a perianal abscess 5 years ago.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHe had painful defecation associated with pain in the perianal region, foul smelling stools and pus discharge in stools. No H\/O blood stained stools. The patient visited the RMP for this as well and it subsided with the medication given by the RMP. Patient developed similar complaints 3 days ago.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENot a known case of Diabetes Mellitus, Hypertension, Epilepsy, Asthma, Tuberculosis, CVA, CAD\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPersonal History -\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EMixed diet\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENormal appetite\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAdequate sleep\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ERegualr Bowel and Bladder Movements\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ERegular intake of alcohol since the past 10 years and chewing on tobacco since the past 3 years.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe patient dropped out of school after finishing 9th standard due to financial troubles and started working at a tiles factory. The patient got married early at the age of 21 years. He started consuming alcohol 10 years ago at the age of 25 years due to peer pressure from his friends. He started by drinking 5ml of sara which gradually increased to 90ml of whiskey and then quarter bottle of whiskey everyday. The patient started chewing tobacco 3 years ago as he feels relieved on chewing tobacco after a tough day at work. He consumes 1-2 packets everyday.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe patient tried to stop consuming alcohol 1 month ago due to pedal oedema and maintained abstinence for 15-20 days by using some herbal medication but was unsuccessful.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe patient last consumed alcohol 5 days ago on Monday before he got hospitalized. He consumed 3 quarters of whiskey on Monday (As he was visiting his different groups of friends)\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;
